title: Variance-Tilted Diffusion Models for Diverse Sampling

paper.title: Variance-Tilted Diffusion Models for Diverse Sampling
paper.abstract: Abstract Diffusion models are typically sampled independently, even when the downstream objective is to obtain a diverse set of candidates. We introduce a variance-weighted batch distribution that favors collections of samples with large empirical spread after a prescribed linear feature map. The target is specified explicitly, and the sampler is derived as the corresponding Doob h h -transform of independent diffusion dynamics. The resulting correction has a compact form: an interaction term that repels posterior denoised means, together with a curvature term that moves particles to the region of higher feature variance. This yields an interacting-particle sampler with a transparent probabilistic target rather than a heuristic repulsive drift.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Diffusion models ( Sohl-Dickstein et al.,, 2015 ; Ho et al.,, 2020 ; Song et al.,, 2020 ) have established themselves as the gold standard for generative modeling, achieving unprecedented fidelity in domains ranging from high-resolution image synthesis ( Dhariwal and Nichol,, 2021 ; Rombach et al., 2022a, ) to scientific discovery, such as protein folding ( Watson et al.,, 2023 ; Abramson et al.,, 2024 ) and molecular docking ( Prat et al.,, 2025 ) . However, the standard sampling paradigm—drawing independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) samples—is often suboptimal for downstream tasks. In many settings, the goal is not merely to generate high-probability modes, but to uncover a set of candidates that covers distinct regions of the data manifold. For instance, in de novo drug design, generating structurally diverse ligands is crucial to mitigate the risk of late-stage failure due to shared toxicity profiles. Similarly, in robotic motion planning, a diverse set of trajectory proposals provides robustness against unforeseen environmental obstacles. To enforce such diversity, approaches such as particle guidance ( Corso et al.,, 2023 ) introduce repulsive potentials into the sampling dynamics. While effective at increasing diversity, these methods modify the drift heuristically, resulting in an implicit target distribution that is computationally intractable to evaluate or control precisely.

sections.heading: Contributions.
sections.text: In contrast to prior work, we define the batch target distribution first and subsequently derive the exact sampler that realizes it. (2) The linear operator A A dictates the representation used to encourage diversity; for example, it can select specific coordinates, isolate low-frequency Fourier coefficients, mask spatial regions, or extract other relevant linear features. Our primary contributions are as follows: • Target-first formulation. We frame diverse generation as an exact sampling problem from the explicit batch target ( 1 ), rather than relying on an uncontrolled repulsive force. • Closed-form Doob correction. We compute the Doob h h -transform induced by the variance tilt and provide the corresponding score correction for a general linear operator A A . • Tractable sampling algorithm. We introduce a discretized interacting-particle sampler. The leading interaction term is computed efficiently using vector-Jacobian products, while the curvature term can be estimated via finite differences or alternative trace/Laplacian estimators. Remark 1.1 . We present our theoretical results under the Variance Exploding (VE) SDE parameterization, as it yields considerably simpler formulas. However, the obtained results readily generalize to other parametrizations (i.e. general linear diffusion models) such as VP-SDEs.

sections.heading: 4 Experiments
sections.text: We evaluate our approach for image generation. In particular, we take Stable Diffusion v1.5 at 512x512 ( Rombach et al., 2022b, ) and apply our variance-tilted Doob h h -transform with the score and posterior mean estimator obtained from classifier-free guidance (CFG) ( Ho and Salimans,, 2022 ) for a variety of different prompts. We test (i) the variance-tilted Doob h h -transform which includes the estimated divergence term and (ii) without the divergence term (i.e. we drop the Tr ( A ⊤ A ∇ s t ) \Tr(A^{\top}A\nabla s_{t}) term from h t A h_{t}^{A} ) against the standard CFG baseline where the initial noise for each approach is set to be the same. We also set A = Id A=\Id . For further details, see Appendix G . We present qualitative results in Figures 1 and 2 . Specifically, we compare the standard CFG baseline against our two proposed configurations: Variance-Tilted ( VT ) without the divergence term, and VT + Divergence , which includes the estimated divergence term. These initial findings are promising and suggest that our variance–weighted distribution achieves meaningful diversity. Rather than simply producing minor variations of high–probability modes, our approach successfully yields a more diverse set of samples that cover a significantly wider range of poses, backgrounds, and visual styles.

sections.heading: 5 Discussion and Conclusion
sections.text: We proposed a target-first approach to diverse diffusion sampling. By reweighting independent samples according to empirical variance after a linear feature map, we obtain an explicit batch distribution and derive its exact Doob correction under Gaussian noising. The resulting sampler has a clear decomposition into denoised-mean repulsion and a curvature correction. This provides a probabilistic alternative to heuristic particle repulsion, while retaining practical implementation paths based on vector-Jacobian products and numerical estimators for the curvature term.

sections.heading: Limitations.
sections.text: While our method qualitatively produces more diverse outputs, it can negatively affect image quality somewhat. Future work could explore how to anneal the Doob correction term to mitigate these effects, as well as quantitatively measuring the performance of our method. Additionally, when including the full divergence term, our method is more expensive than standard sampling from diffusion models due to the cost of estimating the divergence. Future work could explore approaches for reducing this cost while retaining diverse sampling.

We introduce a variance-weighted batch distribution that favors collections of samples with large empirical spread after a prescribed linear feature map. The target is specified explicitly, and the sampler is derived as the corresponding Doob h h -transform of independent diffusion dynamics. The resulting correction has a compact form: an interaction term that repels posterior denoised means, together with a curvature term that moves particles to the region of higher feature variance. This yields an interacting-particle sampler with a transparent probabilistic target rather than a heuristic repulsive drift. Keywords: Machine Learning, Diffusion Models, Diverse Sampling 1 Introduction Diffusion models ( Sohl-Dickstein et al.,, 2015 ; Ho et al.,, 2020 ; Song et al.,, 2020 ) have established themselves as the gold standard for generative modeling, achieving unprecedented fidelity in domains ranging from high-resolution image synthesis ( Dhariwal and Nichol,, 2021 ; Rombach et al., 2022a, ) to scientific discovery, such as protein folding ( Watson et al.,, 2023 ; Abramson et al.,, 2024 ) and molecular docking ( Prat et al.,, 2025 ) . However, the standard sampling paradigm—drawing independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) samples—is often suboptimal for downstream tasks. In many settings, the goal is not merely to generate high-probability modes, but to uncover a set of candidates that covers distinct regions of the data manifold. For instance, in de novo drug design, generating structurally diverse ligands is crucial to mitigate the risk of late-stage failure due to shared toxicity profiles. Similarly, in robotic motion planning, a diverse set of trajectory proposals provides robustness against unforeseen environmental obstacles. To enforce such diversity, approaches such as particle guidance ( Corso et al.,, 2023 ) introduce repulsive potentials into the sampling dynamics. While effective at increasing diversity, these methods modify the drift heuristically, resulting in an implicit target distribution that is computationally intractable to evaluate or control precisely. Our primary contributions are as follows: • Target-first formulation. We frame diverse generation as an exact sampling problem from the explicit batch target ( 1 ), rather than relying on an uncontrolled repulsive force. • Closed-form Doob correction. We compute the Doob h h -transform induced by the variance tilt and provide the corresponding score correction for a general linear operator A A . • Tractable sampling algorithm. We introduce a discretized interacting-particle sampler. The leading interaction term is computed efficiently using vector-Jacobian products, while the curvature term can be estimated via finite differences or alternative trace/Laplacian estimators. Specifically, we compare the standard CFG baseline against our two proposed configurations: Variance-Tilted ( VT ) without the divergence term, and VT + Divergence , which includes the estimated divergence term. These initial findings are promising and suggest that our variance–weighted distribution achieves meaningful diversity. Rather than simply producing minor variations of high–probability modes, our approach successfully yields a more diverse set of samples that cover a significantly wider range of poses, backgrounds, and visual styles. 5 Discussion and Conclusion We proposed a target-first approach to diverse diffusion sampling. By reweighting independent samples according to empirical variance after a linear feature map, we obtain an explicit batch distribution and derive its exact Doob correction under Gaussian noising. The resulting sampler has a clear decomposition into denoised-mean repulsion and a curvature correction. This provides a probabilistic alternative to heuristic particle repulsion, while retaining practical implementation paths based on vector-Jacobian products and numerical estimators for the curvature term. Limitations. While our method qualitatively produces more diverse outputs, it can negatively affect image quality somewhat. Future work could explore how to anneal the Doob correction term to mitigate these effects, as well as quantitatively measuring the performance of our method. Additionally, when including the full divergence term, our method is more expensive than standard sampling from diffusion models due to the cost of estimating the divergence. Future work could explore approaches for reducing this cost while retaining diverse sampling.
